question.problem: The remainder of dividing $q(x)=2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-4x-5$ by $x-2$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The remainder theorem states that when $q(x)$ is divided by $(x-2),$ the remainder equals $q(2).$ 

Evaluating $q(2)$ directly gives

$$
\begin{aligned}q(2) & =2(2)^{3}+(2)^{2}-4(2)-5 \\  & =16+4-8-5 \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

So, when $q(x)$ is divided by $(x-2),$ the remainder is $7.$

**Note:** We can check the answer by carrying out synthetic division:

|  | ${x}^{3}$ | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | $2$ | $1$ | $-4$ | $-5$ |
|  | $↓$ | $4$ | $10$ | $12$ |
|  | $2$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ |
